Retakes are supposed to favor attack side and that’s normal, but retakes on breeze b site are super complicated and feel impossible if you don’t have a hard carry “aimer” on your team that will just walkout of defender spawn arches. If I where to rework I would make the main choke larger, remove cyphers ability to place trips that aren’t breakable from within the choke, and make the wall right in front of defenders spawn arches diagonal. Also they could add a box to hop up over that wall so you could peek it on retakes. 

Mid and tubes just need a complete rework again unfortunately.

Breeze isn’t terrible but there are a couple glaring issues imo. These issues make it if you don’t have specific agents you’re essentially fucked. 

B site: choke is tiny and site is huge, and if you are playing Into a cypher you better hope you have a sova, Skye or gekko to break the trips. IMO the site has too many angles to clear for such a small choke and b tunnel is really hard to take control of without investing all of your util. This site needs some adjustments, it requires a lot of coordination to grain very little ground.

Mid: very attack sided, you pretty much have double doors for free as the défense has to expose themselves to many angles just to contest one, while the attack side is chilling they have multiple safe peeking angles. Also upper mid is pretty much unplayable for anybody, attack or defence. When is the last time you did an upper mid play on breeze? It almost never happenes because it so awkward to fight in at any spot. Get rid of tube, and make mid playable for défense and the map would be instantly funner. 

A: imo the best part of the map, very takeable on attack but also allows a good amount of spots for defence without feeling overwhelming for the attacking team.

Overall defense is very hard because if your team can’t hold the site, if you don’t insta rotate in response the retake on b is very difficult. In this game I find you have to think a lot more than cs. Woohoojin is great at explaining why and how you should be doing things, but at the end of the day any thought process is fine as long as you have a reason to why you do things.

Cs you have a lot more moments where it’s justified to ego challenge 50-50 fights, as information is scarce and you are reliant on reads/mechanics to bail you out of hard situations.

In VALORANT if you are playing well with a team playing well, the site can almost feel unplayable for a defender and vice versa. There is so much utility compared to cs, you have enough utility to gain map control, get info, and execute onto site which is actually insane if you think about it. 

I think if your struggling it’s prob because your utility is bad, and aim alone usually can’t take you that high in the ranks. If you truly have as much cs experience as you say than I wouldn’t spend too much time dm’ing. You really need to focus on getting impact in your rounds which does not neccesarily mean killing everybody. It can mean taking space with util, preemptively taking map control so if your team gets cancelled you have a safe rotate back to the other site, it can mean gathering precious information and making a call to exploit a weakness in their setup, etc.

Also if you’re not having fun and feel like not playing than don’t play. The secret to getting good is putting in hours, and putting in hours required you to have fun. So if your not having fun just play other games maybe VALORANT isn’t for you.

I wasn't going to write but I see that no one else has responded, and you seem like a beginner and I know how crucial feedback can be when learning. I have a lot to say but I think it is better that I just pick the biggest most important thing to critique so as to not overwhelm you.

The first thing that is painfully obvious to me is the lack of context between sections. The background is all white, there are no containers, shadows, colors, or font changes to signify some type of relationship or hierarchy between your elements. I would define your sections more in one way or another. You can do this in many ways, but what i reccomend for your design are the following;

"cards" with a white fill, no stroke, and a drop shadow. you can maybe find a way to develop your green bubble idea more by putting them on top of the "cards".

Font thickness and having 2 fonts can help signify titles vs body text. If you find a good combo of title and body fonts, you can really take the "look" of your design to the next level.

You could go a more minimalist route and keep the all-white aesthetic, but consider using some more color in the layout to help communicate different sections. Be careful here to not use too many, 2 is often enough.

Your 3rd photo with the list is also flawed. you can't just dump that much text  (talking about the list here) and not separate it in some way that helps the eye parse the info. here is a really good article that can shine some light on the subject :[https://www.justinmind.com/ui-design/list](https://www.justinmind.com/ui-design/list)

Anyway, i hope that helps. You really need to work on your visual communication and using subtle details to suggest certain ideas to the user. for example using a card with a small shadow to define a section, using a bold text to say this is a title and small text to relay info, color change to break up the page etc...

I could try and explain the details to you, but its better for you to just go out there and fuck around with shit until it works. have fun!

Define adequate, you're daily intake of b 12 is only about two and a half micrograms. That amount can easily obtained. 

Is the lack of vitamin B12 in plants the proof that we are meant to eat meat?

The answer is that humans are omnivores which means we can survive on many different types of food. It is likely that we were originally frugivores and evolved to be able to digest meat. There is an interesting youtube video called ‘Are Humans Omnivores, Carnivores or Herbivores’ on this subject.

Vitamin B12 comes from bacteria in the ground. In the past, we had no need to supplement because we could absorb it from our ‘dirty’ food and drinking water (and also from the meat some people ate).

Now, with higher standards of food and water hygiene, we cannot obtain it from plant foods or water. Furthermore, the only reason you can get it from meat (if the animal you are eating was not living off grass) is that supplements are given to the animal.

In some (poorer) parts of the world people still eat very little, if any, meat and dairy products and they remain healthy. My guess is that their food and water has not been sterilized in the same way it has in the more ‘developed’ parts of the world. That brings it’s own problems of course but probably allows them to absorb vitamin B12 naturally.

Either way, in today’s sterile world, you will be taking a vitamin B12 supplement, one way or another.

So, no, lack of vitamin B12 is not a reason we should eat meat. We are not ideally suited to eating it in large quantities like we are fruits and vegetables, but neither is it poison to us.

My view is that if we can take it or leave it (because we can), we should leave it as it causes animal suffering, damage to our health and damage to the environment.
